utility.value: City of Mesa Energy Resources Department (Mesa Electric, municipal utility)
utility.notes: Mesa operates its own municipal electric utility for part of the city; the utility's own Solar Program page explicitly states 'SRP customers, please visit SRP's website' — confirming Mesa is genuinely split between two separate electric providers depending on address, similar to Phoenix's APS/SRP split. This record is scoped to Mesa's own municipal electric service area only; SRP-served Mesa addresses are NOT covered by this record and should not be assumed to follow the same interconnection/net-metering process.

value.name: City of Mesa Energy Resources Department
value.notes: Municipal net metering program (FY25-26): Mesa purchases excess PV generation from qualified net metering customers on a monthly basis, applied as a bill credit; no CCA applicable (municipal utility, not investor-owned). Initial credit rate is determined by the date of customer interconnection, per Mesa's own Solar Program page — a specific numeric rate was not published on this page and was not independently found this session.

permit_authority.value: City of Mesa Development Services Department, Permit Services (construction permit only where triggered); City of Mesa Energy Resources Department (interconnection)
permit_authority.notes: Genuinely distinct from Phoenix and Tucson: Mesa's own Residential Construction FAQ states directly, 'solar power systems under 10,000 square feet that are certified by a recognized agency and installed by a licensed Arizona contractor... do not need a construction permit. However, new electric meters or circuits will require a permit.' So most residential rooftop solar in Mesa does not go through the City's DIMES building-permit process at all unless the installation adds a new electric meter or circuit — the substantive gatekeeping step is Energy Resources' interconnection application, not a construction permit. This is a real, city-specific difference, not an assumption; recorded verbatim from Mesa's own page rather than inferred from Phoenix/Tucson's pattern.

battery_programs.notes: Mesa's Solar Program page sets a higher system-size allowance for systems WITH storage (see eligibility_constraints) but does not describe a separate battery incentive/rebate program; left null rather than inferred.

value.name: Plan submittal (spec sheet, protection equipment, electrical three-line, control schematics and connection diagrams, signage and labeling, as one uploaded file)

required_documents.notes: Per Mesa Energy Resources' own Solar Program page (interconnection application checklist, Step 1).

inspection_steps.notes: Mesa's Solar Program page requires a roof photo of the completed PV system prior to interconnection but does not describe a formal City building-inspection procedure, consistent with most Mesa solar installs not requiring a construction permit at all (see permit_authority notes); left unresolved rather than inferred.

value.program_or_pathway: Mesa Energy Resources interconnection application (net metering)
other_conditions: Residential systems WITHOUT storage: module capacity may not exceed 5 kW and inverter capacity may not exceed 5 kW
Residential systems WITH storage: module capacity may not exceed 10 kW and inverter capacity may not exceed 11.5 kW
Inverter capacity limits are based on rated capability, not programmed output — derating a higher-rated inverter to comply is explicitly not permitted
PV modules and inverters must be on the California SB1-approved equipment list
Installer must hold an eligible Arizona contractor license classification (e.g. B-, C-05 Solar, CR-11/R-11, KB-1, KB-2, KO- Solar, K-05 Solar, K-11, or other City-approved license)
Inverter must be UL 1741 compliant; all equipment UL-listed
Customer is solely responsible for obtaining any permits/inspections/approvals required by applicable jurisdictions
Applications must be received and accepted for interconnection prior to installation

permit_fees.notes: Neither the Solar Program page nor the Residential Construction FAQ published a specific solar interconnection or permit fee amount this session; not guessed.
